name: Easy Pressure Cooker Fish Chowder with Potatoes, Fennel, Corn, Bacon & Sourdough

instructions.primary_message: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Trim off root end and stalks of the fennel, leaving only the white bulbs. Halve fennel bulbs lengthwise and medium dice. Place in a medium bowl.
Set a 6-quart electric pressure cooker to sauté on HIGH.
While the cooker heats up, peel, halve, and medium dice onion. Add to the bowl with the fennel.

Once the pressure cooker insert is hot, add butter and swirl to coat the bottom. Add fennel, onion, salt, and pepper; cook, stirring occasionally, until starting to soften, 5-6 minutes. (Reserve bowl for the next step.)
instructions.secondary_message:
butter, unsalted
1 tsp salt
½ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Meanwhile, slide thyme leaves off the stems; discard the stems. Large dice potatoes. Place both in the reserved bowl.

When the fennel and onion are soft, add thyme, potatoes, broth, and corn. Stir to combine, then lock lid and set to pressure cook on HIGH for 3 minutes. When the chowder is done, allow the pressure to release naturally for 10 minutes, then manually drape a clean towel over the vent. Carefully release any remaining pressure and remove lid.
instructions.secondary_message:
6 cups vegetable broth
2 cups frozen corn

instructions.primary_message: While the pressure is releasing, cut cod into bite-sized pieces.
When the pressure has released, add cod to the pressure cooker, then set to sauté on HIGH. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the cod is cooked through, 3-5 minutes.
Add cream and stir once more to combine.
Divide chowder between bowls and top with bacon bits. Serve with buttered bread on the side and enjoy!
instructions.secondary_message:
⅔ cup bacon bits
butter, unsalted
5 slice sourdough bread
